meta.factIdFormat: src/brief/selfcheck.ts factId(fact) = `${fact.id}:${fact.file}${fact.line===undefined?'':':'+fact.line}`. This file stores `id` (the detector id, e.g. "coupling.missing") and `file`/`line` separately; bench/verify/run.ts must compose factId itself the same way selfcheck.ts does, to match a labelled fact against scoreDiff's live output.

meta.discrepancy: contract.env: the research note's fact-type table says "Fired 2, True+useful 2", but only ONE contract.env fire is traceable in the six notes and in fastlane's raw JSON dump (notes/raw/env-30112.brief.json has exactly one contract.env fact). No second contract.env fire is named or quoted anywhere in the available material — grepped all six .md notes and all fastlane raw/*.brief.json files for 'contract.env' / env-var language and found nothing beyond env-30112. This is the ONLY unresolved gap: every other fact-type row (contract.api 10/8/2/0, contract.dependency 7/5/0/2, layers.edge 1/0/1/0, coupling.missing 18/0/18/0) reconciles exactly against what the six notes describe, including the black 1ed66a8 PR's known 'unreconciled' 4th fact (see that PR's facts below, label 'unclassified'). Flagged for the lead rather than guessed at; do not fabricate a second contract.env fact to force the total to 15 true-useful.

setupQuirks.fastlane: Ran with history.maxCommits: 1500 and history.lookbackDays: 90 set locally, and a FULL (non-shallow, non-blobless) clone. Default config (history.maxCommits: 20000) crashed outright on every PR before tuning: opendrs's git() wrapper has a fixed 120s per-invocation timeout with no --max-commits/--since override on brief/score, and a raw `git log -n20000 --name-status -M` took 7m47s wall-clock (1.78s user + 2.92s system CPU) on the contended field-test host. A bench run against fastlane MUST set these two config keys (or run.ts hard-codes them for the fastlane repo entry) and must NOT use a blobless/--filter=blob:none clone — the note explicitly says this makes fastlane's raw SCORE numbers (not its fact/detector findings) non-comparable to the other five repos.
setupQuirks.cli-cli: cli/cli's history rarely carries a GitHub PR number on trunk (only 9 of 276 sampled commits do). 3 of its 8 rows are commit-range stand-ins picked via `git log --shortstat` rather than real PRs (091c24d70, 62a6e9e05, and the third is PR-backed per the note's own table — re-check: the note's table shows all 8 rows with PR# except 091c24d70 and 62a6e9e05 marked 'n/a*'; the note's header text says '3 of its 8 rows are commit-range stand-ins' but only 2 are visibly marked n/a in the per-PR table — this is itself an unreconciled count inside the source note, flagged here rather than silently resolved). base=sha~1, head=sha for every row regardless.
setupQuirks.otherFive: black, actix-web, vite and vapor ran default opendrs config on `--filter=blob:none` (blobless) clones. cli-cli was also blobless but needed one retry on its first `score` call (a benign git auto-packing message was misread as a fatal error by the 120s-timeout git wrapper).

knownCaveats: ArchitectureFact (src/domain/types.ts) carries only {id, weight, file, line?, text} — no partner file, no per-fact index. Several coupling.missing facts that fire on the SAME file (e.g. vite 77d837351's 10 facts, all on the renovate-bumped template's package.json) therefore share one identical factId. This labels file lists each field-test-counted instance separately (with a `partner` field where the note names one) for traceability, but bench/verify/run.ts and the lead's recall/precision scoring MUST decide how to count a collapsed factId against several distinct labelled instances — recommend treating a collapsed id as satisfied if ANY of its labelled instances' expected action is produced, and flagging the collapse itself as a product gap, not working around it silently.

black's own PR 1ed66a8 is credited with 4 facts in its per-PR table but the note's per-fact judgment section only individually discusses 3 (two contract.api, one coupling.missing) — the note says explicitly it does not know what the 4th fact was (docs/research/2026-10-19-field-test.md, 'What could not be reconciled'). Recorded below with label "unclassified" so the per-PR fact count (4) still reconciles; excluded from recall/precision targets.

Several `file` values below are best-reading inferences, not values quoted verbatim in the note (the notes describe facts in prose, not raw JSON, except for fastlane which has notes/raw/*.json). Each such entry has `ambiguous: true` and a `note` explaining the inference.

Line numbers are included only where the note states them verbatim (actix-web gives explicit file:line for 2 facts; fastlane's raw JSON gives exact file:line for both of its facts). Everywhere else `line` is omitted, not guessed.
